sections.h2: Where is Crown Point, Indiana, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Crown Point is the county seat of Lake County in northwest Indiana, about 40 miles southeast of the Chicago Loop. The city covers roughly 18 square miles and sits on the Valparaiso Moraine, at an elevation near 717 feet.

Merrillville lies to the north, Winfield to the east, Cedar Lake to the southwest and St. John to the west. The city spans two townships, Center and Ross, and that split matters to a seller because it decides which school corporation a buyer's children would attend.

Almost all residents, 99.2%, live in areas the census classes as urban. Crown Point is a suburb with a historic square at its center rather than a small town surrounded by farms.

sections.h2: What is the history of Crown Point?
sections.html:
Solon Robinson and his family were the first settlers, arriving on October 31, 1834. Lake County was organized in 1837, and Robinson later paid for a $500 wooden courthouse in Crown Point, which helped the town win the county seat.

Crown Point incorporated as a town in 1868 and as a city on June 6, 1911. Construction on the large courthouse that still stands on the square began in 1878, with additions through 1928. The building went onto the National Register of Historic Places in 1974, and the county moved into a new Government Center in 1975.

  • 1896: William Jennings Bryan spoke from the courthouse steps.
  • 1909: Louis Chevrolet won the first Cobe Trophy race here.
  • 1934: John Dillinger escaped from the county jail on March 3.
  • Marriage Mill: the city earned that nickname because it had no marriage license waiting period.

The Courthouse Square, Sunnyside and Holley historic districts are all in Crown Point. A home inside one of them may carry design review rules, and Indiana's seller disclosure form asks the owner to say whether the property lies in a locally designated historic district.

sections.h2: What do the census numbers say about Crown Point housing?
sections.html:
Crown Point is a homeowner city. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 85.5% for 2020 to 2024, with a median owner-occupied value of $294,800 and median gross rent of $1,485.

With so few rentals, a house that needs work stands out on a street of well-kept homes. Buyers financing with a mortgage often ask for repairs before closing, which is one reason owners with dated kitchens, old roofs or deferred maintenance look at a direct as-is sale.

The 2025 estimate for the city is 35,616 residents, so the growth seen in the last census has continued.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Crown Point homes?
sections.html:
Two public school corporations serve the city. Crown Point Community School Corporation serves residents of Center Township, and Merrillville Community School Corporation serves residents of Ross Township.

Public schools named in the city include Crown Point High School and the Robert A. Taft and Colonel John Wheeler middle schools. Private options include Pathway Christian School, Trinity Lutheran School, St. Mary Catholic Community School and Avicenna Academy.

When you sell, expect buyers to ask which township the house is in. Your listing or cash buyer can confirm the district from the property address.

sections.h2: What are the main roads, rail and attractions near Crown Point?
sections.html:
The Crown Point Sportsplex, a 95-acre outdoor sports complex, sits off I-65, the interstate that serves the city.

Passenger rail is a short drive away. Wikipedia reports that the Munster/Dyer South Shore Line station opened on March 31, 2026, and that residents also use the Gary Metro Center and East Chicago stations. Gary Public Transportation Corporation runs buses along the 93rd Avenue corridor.

  • Lake County Fairgrounds: the Lake County Fair runs ten days each early August and is described as the second-largest county fair in Indiana.
  • Crown Point Bridge: an 85-foot covered bridge built in 1878 in Rush County and moved to the fairgrounds in 1933.
  • Festivals: the Corn Roast, Taste of Crown Point, and parades on Memorial Day, July 4 and St. Patrick's Day.

Proximity to Chicago, about 40 miles away, and to the rail stations above is worth mentioning when you describe the house to any buyer.

sections.h2: How does a house sale work in Lake County, Indiana?
sections.html:
A deed for a Crown Point home is recorded with the Lake County Recorder in Crown Point, and the office handles deeds, mortgages, liens and releases. It sits in Building A, second floor, 2293 N. Main Street, Crown Point, and is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. The phone number is 219-755-3730.

Indiana also expects a sales disclosure form for a transfer of residential property. The Indiana Code defines the conveyance documents that fall under that rule, and it excludes items such as mortgages, short leases and certain quitclaim deeds. Your closing company normally prepares the form with the deed.

For most residential sales, Indiana also requires the owner to complete a state disclosure form. It covers the foundation, mechanical systems, roof, structure, and water and sewer systems, plus methamphetamine contamination, flood plain knowledge and historic district status. A buyer purchasing as-is still sees this form, so fill it in honestly.

  • Order a payoff statement from your lender.
  • Confirm the township and school corporation.
  • Check for unpaid property tax with the Lake County Treasurer.
  • Choose a title or closing company.

sections.h2: When are Crown Point property taxes due, and what happens if they are missed?
sections.html:
Indiana property tax is paid in two installments. Indiana Code 6-1.1-22-9 sets the dates as May 10 and November 10, and the state's 2026 list shows May 11 and November 10.

A payment up to 30 days late carries a 5% penalty, and one more than 30 days late carries 10%, according to the Department of Local Government Finance. Lake County taxes are paid to the Treasurer at 2293 N. Main Street in Crown Point, phone 219-755-3760.

If a parcel stays delinquent, the county can offer it at a tax sale. Lake County compiles its delinquent list by July 1 or 51 days after the due date, adds a tax sale charge, mails certified letters and publishes owner names in two local newspapers. The sale is held online, and the minimum bid is the full amount owed on the parcel. Owners who want details on redeeming a parcel can call the Auditor at 219-755-3155.

If you owe back taxes and are thinking of selling, clearing them from the sale proceeds at closing is a common route. Do it before the sale list is certified if you can.

sections.h2: What do Crown Point sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Crown Point has a median owner-occupied value of $294,800, so many owners hold real equity. The pressure on a sale usually comes from time, repairs or an estate.

  • An inherited house in Lake County that must pass through probate before it can be sold.
  • A home that needs a new roof, furnace or foundation work that would show up on a buyer's inspection.
  • Landlords exiting a rental in a city where most homes are owner-occupied.
  • Owners relocating who cannot carry two mortgages while waiting for a listing to sell.

A cash offer removes the lender appraisal and the repair negotiation. It will usually come in below a fully renovated retail sale, so compare it with the net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and ask for the terms in writing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Crown Point house?
faqs.a: With the Lake County Recorder, 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor, Crown Point. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone number is 219-755-3730.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Crown Point?
faqs.a: In two installments, in May and November. The Indiana Department of Local Government Finance lists May 11 and November 10 for 2026, with a 5% penalty for payments up to 30 days late and 10% after that.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Crown Point house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the township. Center Township addresses are served by Crown Point Community School Corporation, and Ross Township addresses are served by Merrillville Community School Corporation.

faqs.q: Do I need to fill out a disclosure form to sell my Crown Point home?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Indiana's residential disclosure form asks the owner about the foundation, roof, mechanical systems, structure, water and sewer, contamination from methamphetamine, flood plain knowledge and historic district status. Ask your closing company whether your sale is exempt.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Crown Point house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, but a parcel that stays delinquent can be listed for the Lake County online tax sale, so it helps to act early.

faqs.q: Is a house in a historic district harder to sell in Crown Point?
faqs.a: It can be. Courthouse Square, Sunnyside and Holley are historic districts, and the seller disclosure asks whether a property sits in a locally designated one, so buyers will want to know about any design rules.
